newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agents charge bogus money scheme at Columbia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agents charge bogus money scheme at Columbia.

text.p: Undercover agents taught several former Ivy League students a lesson by breaking up a money printing scheme they were allegedly operating out of a basement at Columbia University.

The U.S. Secret Service charged that for the past six months four young men counterfeited more than $80,000 in $20 bills, passing them in bars, restaurants and smoke shops and selling them to other people in New York, Chicago and Washington.

Last week's arrests were announced on Monday night and a complaint filed in Manhattan Federal Court alleged the defendants -- three former students at Columbia and a fourth who had returned to work in a printing office in the Graduate School of Journalism building -- used a university-owned colour copier and specially treated paper to print the bills.

"They were fair copies," said Brian Gimlett, the special agent in charge of the Secret Service New York field office. "They spent some time in preparation to make these. They were trying to duplicate the appearance of genuine notes."
The copier in the basement of the journalism school is normally used for making faculty reports, student newsletters and university administration documents.

While the amount of fake money printed was not large by the standard of mass-produced counterfeit schemes, making bogus money on the Columbia campus was unprecedented. University officials cooperated in the investigation.
The four suspects were arrested last week and agents found a backpack full of counterfeit $20 bills and a paper cutter in the apartment shared by two of the former students.

According to the complaint, Secret Service agents obtained counterfeit money in a bar in New York in May and traced it to the copier at Columbia. An informant arranged meetings between the suspects and undercover agents, who were present when various exchanges of the counterfeit bills for real money were made between the defendants.
